title: Havenly Fintech on‑prem cutover & Terraform notes (WIP)
content:
Context:
Havenly Fintech (Havenly) is doing an initial cutover from Hosted->Private (on‑prem + customer VPC peering) for fraud‑scoring and customer support embeddings. They requested a hardened, FIPS‑adjacent setup with HSM/KMS integration, predictable latency (99th pct < 120ms per request under 200 TPS), and an upgrade path that minimizes risk to trading hours (09:30–16:00 local).

Goals for this playbook (scope):
- Provide a recommended node/GPU/Network sizing for production (99th pct targets + buffer).
- Terraform module notes and state management guidance for their infra team.
- Stepwise cutover/upgrade plan (dry runs, canary, rollback).
- Open questions for security/compliance and action owners.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline traffic: 150 TPS steady with 50 TPS burst windows (2x bursts during marketing).
- Average request sequence length: 256 tokens; 90th pct <= 512 tokens.
- Model: 13B dense transformer variant (quantized) with 1.5–2ms per-token GPU performance on A300/A10G class for our runtime.
- Latency SLO target end‑to‑end: 120 ms at p99 for typical prompts (~40 tokens).
- Customer will provide 3 racks with redundant spine switches, 100GbE fabric inside datacenter.
- Customer has on‑prem virtualization and supports Kubernetes v1.26+.
- KMS: Thales HSM via KMIP (customer requirement).

Suggested topology (high level):
- Control plane (Redwood components): 3 nodes (VMs) in management subnet (customer-managed), privately peered with their control network. RBAC restricted to corporate IPs + Redwood ops VPN.
- Serving plane: Kubernetes cluster dedicated to inference. Namespace isolation per environment (prod/stage/canary).
- Node types:
  - GPU worker (inference): 6x nodes with 80 GB GPU RAM equivalent (A100/A30 equivalent). Each node: 8x 80GB GPUs OR 4x A100 40GB depending on customer hardware availability.
  - CPU worker (aux services): 3x m8-like nodes for encoder/IO/sidecars, 64 vCPU, 512 GB RAM.
  - Storage nodes: 3x nodes with NVMe mirrored (20 TB usable) for model artifacts and KV cache.
- Network: L7 LB in front of runtime, internal clustering over 25Gb or 100Gb depending on rack; we recommend 100Gb between GPU nodes for large KV cache transfers during rollout.

Sizing rationale (quick math):
- Target throughput: 200 TPS sustained during peak.
- Per-request estimated token alignment: 40 tokens per request * 200 TPS = 8k tokens/s = 480k tokens/min.
- Runtime per token on quantized model: 0.75–1.5ms token/GPU-band (varies) -> conservatively 1ms => 8k ms-equivalent GPU ops/s -> ~8 concurrent token‑ops pipelines.
- Based on internal benchmarks, a single A100x4 node (4 GPUs 40GB) sustains ~70–90 prompt TPS for 40 token requests with proper batching. So 3 such nodes provide ~240 TPS with buffer. Hence proposal: 4 GPU-worker nodes (4x40GB GPUs) for primary cluster + 2 for spare/failover -> 6 nodes total.

Capacity & HA notes:
- We want at least N+2 for GPU workers (N=4 active, +2 spare) to survive one host failure and allow rolling upgrades.
- Control plane: 3 nodes across different racks. etcd (or equivalent store) should have dedicated disks and snapshot schedule (hourly, retain 7 days).
- KV cache persisted locally but checkpointed to storage every 10 minutes; warmup scripts included in the playbook.

Terraform notes (module-level):
- Terraform version: pin to 1.5.x (customer standard uses 1.5.6).
- Providers: aws (for S3-like object store), kubernetes, helm, external. Pin provider versions in root module.
- Remote state: use customer S3-compatible objectstore + locking with Dynamo/etcd (customer uses HashiCorp Vault + Consul — we will recommend Consul for locking if customer already runs it). Provide example backend snippet.
- Module layout (recommended):
  - network/vpc module (subnets, route tables, NACLs)
  - compute/k8s cluster module (node pools, autoscaling groups, machine images)
  - security/iam-kms module (HSM endpoints, IAM roles, service accounts)
  - storage/kv-artifacts module (persistent volumes, object-store creds)
  - runtime/redwood module (Helm chart install values, CRs for model pinning)
- Naming conventions: redwood-<customer>-<env>-<component> (lowercase, max 32 chars).
- TF state file layout: one state per major module group (network, cluster, security) to limit blast radius.
- Secrets handling: use Vault for secrets injection; do not store KMS keys in TF variables. Use data sources + Vault transforms.
- Upgrade note: provider upgrades must be run in a sandbox workspace first. Provider major version changes require manual plan review.

Example TF backend snippet (to give to customer):
- backend "s3" {
    bucket = "<customer-redwood-tfstate>"
    key    = "prod/network/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-east-1"
    dynamodb_table = "tfstate-locks"
  }
(If no S3, swap to onprem MinIO + Consul lock using consul backend.)

Cluster and Helm values (notes):
- model image are pinned to SHA tags; never use latest.
- replicas: start with 3 replicas for the runtime controller, scale to 5 in heavy mode.
- resource requests/limits: we provide recommended YAML snippets in the repo.
- readinessProbe: extended to 90s during cold start windows to avoid false failovers.

Cutover & upgrade plan (high level phases):
Phase 0 — Preflight (2–3 weeks before cutover)
- Inventory: ensure hardware procurement + firmware versions compatible.
- Security: HSM endpoints verified and handshake tested.
- Dry-run TF apply in staging environment that mirrors prod network.
- Team playthrough: incident channel, runbook accessible, pager ops rotated.
- Acceptance test suite created (latency + functional prompts).

Phase 1 — Canary deployment (day −2 to day −1)
- Deploy runtime to canary namespace with 1 GPU node pool (1–2 GPUs).
- Mirror 1% traffic via proxy (or replay traces) for 4–6 hours.
- Run synthetic load: 20 TPS sustained, validate p99 latencies and cost numbers.

Phase 2 — Gradual traffic shift (cutover day)
- Pre‑window backup: snapshot control plane + PVs, export TF plan.
- Shift traffic 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% in 30–60 minute intervals. Validate SLOs at each step.
- If p99 goes over threshold for 2 consecutive intervals: rollback to previous route and mark a postmortem.

Phase 3 — Post cutover (day +1 to +7)
- Monitor error rates, tail latencies, and cost signals.
- Run a resync of cached artifacts and KV warming (precompute top prefixes).
- Schedule a minor patch window (no model changes) at +72 hours.

Rollback plan (concise):
- Quick rollback path: revert routing at L7 to Hosted or previous cluster pool (we maintain a standby route to Hosted for 48 hrs post cutover).
- State restore: restore etcd snapshot from t-1 hour if cluster state corrupted.
- Model rollback: redeploy pinned image SHA from pre-cutover registry snapshot.

Open questions (must resolve before final):
- KMS: Does Havenly require HSM‑backed key wrapping for all tokens or only for long lived secrets? Owner: Priya Nair (sec).
- Network: Are there any network ACLs or egress restrictions between racks that would throttle KV cache transfer? Need topology diagram from customer netops. Owner: Ethan Brooks.
- Disaster recovery: What is RTO requirement for control plane (24 hrs? 4 hrs?). This affects etcd snapshot cadence and number of control nodes. Owner: Maya Chen.
- Compliance: Any additional encryption-at-rest policies that require FIPS-certified libraries in our runtime containers? Owner: Diego Alvarez.

Unresolved technical risks and mitigations:
- Risk: KV cache warmup on first traffic spike will cause high tail latency. Mitigation: pre-warm popular prefixes and use staged rollout of models; increase readinessProbe window to account for cold starts.
- Risk: Terraform state drift between customer and Redwood-managed modules. Mitigation: establish a shared ownership model for TF state, weekly drift detection job that runs plan-only.

Checklist (pre‑cutover):
- [ ] Hardware final checksum + firmware version confirmation
- [ ] TF state backend provisioned and locked for prod
- [ ] Vault paths and service principal for Redwood ops validated
- [ ] Canary test report signed off by customer SRE
- [ ] HSM KMIP handshake tested end-to-end

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: get network topology + ACL export from Havenly netops (due 2025-01-20)
- Priya: confirm HSM key wrapping requirements and coordinate with compliance (due 2025-01-22)
- Diego: run provider upgrade sandbox test and report incompatibilities (due 2025-01-24)
- Maya: prepare final TF module checklist and version locks (due 2025-01-28)

Notes to self / rough TODOs (internal):
- Add script to automate KV cache checkpointing and recovery (link to repo PR).
- Draft runbook for model hot rollback that doesn't require cluster reboot.
- Confirm monitoring thresholds (we currently use 95ms/120ms/200ms tiers).

Appendix: quick model warmup snippet (bash)
- for prefix in $(cat top-1k-prefixes.txt); do 
    curl -X POST https://runtime-internal.local/warm -d "{"prefix":"$prefix"}" &
  done

End of WIP. Keep this doc as the single source for cutover decisions until final approved playbook is checked into the private-deploy repo.
